public_rationale: Apple's May 2022 guide describes iOS and iPadOS app sandboxing, and its May 16, 2023 disclosure describes automated checks and human app review [e2, e3]. OpenAI's March 23, 2023 announcement describes a sandboxed, firewalled code interpreter [e1]. Researchers reported no observed anonymization of user input in a June 7, 2023 Clinical Trial Radar interaction; the cited research version became available July 26, 2024 [e4]. These sources document safeguards and a privacy concern, but do not establish equivalent security boundaries or a complete comparison of contemporary review and enforcement [e1–e4]. They therefore neither establish nor refute the claimed system-wide difference during March 23–June 8, 2023 [e1–e4].
limitations: The packet lacks a sufficiently complete account of OpenAI's review and enforcement during the target period.
Device-app sandboxing and hosted-tool isolation are not compared using a common security boundary or measure.
One plugin interaction does not establish system-wide behavior; code-interpreter safeguards do not establish protections for all third-party plugins.
Company descriptions do not independently establish safeguard effectiveness.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Marcus says he does not see any reason to think ChatGPT plugins are in fact safe, noting that they are far less sandboxed and less rigorously controlled than Apple App Store apps.

statement.excerpt: I don’t see any reason to think these plugins are in fact safe. (They are far less sandboxed and less rigorously controlled than Apple app store apps.)
statement.document_title: Two models of AI oversight - and how things could go deeply wrong

from_speaker: I don’t see any reason to think these plugins are in fact safe
less rigorously controlled than Apple app store apps
our_interpretation: The checkable commitment is the comparison of safeguards. Marcus’s statement about his own confidence is not independently measurable.
The plain reading is that the contemporary ChatGPT plugin system imposed substantially weaker isolation and review controls than Apple’s App Store system.
Assess the initial plugin deployment through the post date. The start is the public plugin launch, because the context concerns the current product rather than a financial reporting period.
Compare enforced isolation, permissions, review and continuing oversight. Neither platform must be entirely free of vulnerabilities.
Distinguish OpenAI-hosted tools from third-party plugins. Their safeguards need not be identical.
criteria.support_condition: Documentation or reproducible analysis of the contemporary systems establishes substantially weaker isolation and less rigorous review or enforcement across the relevant ChatGPT plugin system.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable documentation or testing establishes that the relevant plugin system had equivalent or stronger isolation or review controls, materially defeating the claimed comparison.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI described concrete isolation for its code interpreter. This is material against treating all plugins as lacking safeguards, but it does not establish equivalent protection across third-party plugins or against Apple's controls.

evidence.locator: App Review section, first process-description paragraph
evidence.explanation: Apple described checks on every submission, including automated checks and human review. This establishes the Apple side of the comparison, but does not measure OpenAI's review rigor.

evidence.locator: Page 100, Security of runtime process in iOS and iPadOS, Sandboxing
evidence.explanation: The guide explains Apple's device-level isolation boundary. It predates the target period and does not compare that boundary with remote plugin services; the availability date is a conservative month-end bound for the May 2022 edition.

evidence.locator: Appendix C.1, Clinical Trial Radar interaction
evidence.publisher: Umar Iqbal, Tadayoshi Kohno and Franziska Roesner via arXiv
evidence.explanation: The researchers dated this interaction to June 7 and reported failure to follow the plugin's anonymization instructions. It substantiates a contemporary privacy concern, but supplies no matched Apple comparison.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Archived requirements and enforcement records for the March 23–June 8, 2023 plugin system, together with matched analysis of isolation, permissions, review and continuing oversight against the relevant Apple platforms.
